evals.prompt: I'm building a PDF text-extraction pipeline in Go. I want to cache results so we don't re-run expensive OCR on the same files every run. My first instinct is to use the file path as the cache key, stored in a map[string]Result. Is this a good approach?
evals.expected_output: Recommends hashing file content (e.g. SHA-256) instead of using the file path as the cache key, explaining that path-based caching breaks when a file is renamed or moved.

assertions.text: Recommends a content hash instead of the file path

evals.prompt: Here's my Go function: func ExtractText(path string, cacheEnabled bool, cacheDir string) (Document, error) — it checks the cache itself before doing extraction. Is this a good design?
evals.expected_output: Flags mixing caching logic into the extraction function as a single-responsibility violation and recommends a separate service-layer wrapper that keeps the extraction function pure.

evals.prompt: In my Go content-hash cache, what should happen if a cache file on disk exists but its JSON is corrupted or unreadable when I try to load it?
evals.expected_output: Recommends treating the corrupted or unreadable cache entry as a cache miss and reprocessing the file, rather than returning an error or crashing.

assertions.text: Recommends treating corruption as a cache miss
Rules out crashing on corrupted cache data
